s01.text: Most days, running Me You Social Publisher is reading one email, or opening one page. The routine is a check, not a shift.

s02.text: If something urgent is waiting, the workspace's admins get one morning digest email listing it, one link per item. A quiet morning sends nothing, on purpose. No email and a green Inbox means genuinely nothing to do.

s03.text: Work the Inbox top to bottom. Approve or request changes on a post. Answer a question in your own words; it is saved to the expert profile and asked once. Verify a claim with a real link, or drop it. Approve or replace a held image. The header count should reach zero.

s04.text: Answer people the day they write. Distribute, then Engage, holds comments, direct messages and reviews in one place. The one hard deadline in the whole app is here: Facebook and Instagram only accept a direct message reply within twenty-four hours.

s05.text: If you would rather not hunt, ask. The Ask button sits on every page. Say what should I do next, and the assistant reads the Inbox, the pipeline, the connections and the dials, ranks the moves, and offers to do each one.

s06.text: It can do nearly everything you can do here. Anything outward-facing or hard to undo is proposed first, as: I am about to. Go ahead? It runs only when you say yes. Every action lands in the audit log. And it will never enter API keys, delete a workspace, or send an email on its own.

s07.text: Five minutes a day. Me You Social Publisher. Your job is decisions, not production.
